output.brief: The crash gap is mostly caused by build 7.4.0, not by the Tiled Canvas flag. Only 7.4.0 users can get the flag, so the flag group is just the 7.4.0 group. Build 7.4.0 crashed at about 2% on 2–3 September, before the flag ramp began. Build 7.3.2 stayed at about 0.7% throughout. The biggest crash cluster in 7.4.0 (41% of events) is in the upgraded image library (Pixelda), and none of the top clusters involves the canvas code. Inside 7.4.0, the random flag-off holdout crashes at 1.98% versus 2.10% with the flag on. That +0.12 point difference is within noise, so a small flag effect (a few tenths of a point) is not ruled out. Device mix and usage are the same in both groups. The app-store console agrees with the crash-reporting SDK, so this is not a counting artifact. The 9 September backend deploy did not move 7.3.2 crash rates. Turning the flag off and releasing 7.4.0 to 100% would leave the main problem in place and close the incident wrongly. Next steps: hold 7.4.0 at 25%, fix the Pixelda HEIF decode crash, and keep the flag holdout running (or widen it) to settle the small flag effect. Confidence is fairly high for the build conclusion and lower for the flag's own small effect.
output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification and distinctions (flag vs. build vs. device vs. usage), then Analysis of Competing Hypotheses and provenance check across the five hypotheses; EDF record kept throughout.
